title: More Than Two Paths
content:
What problem does this solve?
A single if can answer one yes-or-no question. The intake desk for the Gloamfen route has three possible outcomes, but the expedition must receive exactly one of them.

Basic syntax
  if supplies >= 10:
      status = "Cleared"
  elif supplies >= 5:
      status = "Review"
  else:
      status = "Denied"

What actually happens
elif means "otherwise, test this next." Python checks conditions top to bottom. The first true branch runs, then the rest of the chain is skipped. With supplies equal to 8, both "not enough for clearance" and "at least 5" feel relevant, but Python stops at the first matching branch.

Order matters
If you put a broad threshold before a stricter one, the stricter branch may never run. Separate if statements can all fire; an if/elif/else chain picks exactly one outcome.

When this is useful
Use elif when several tiers are possible and the program must assign exactly one result.
concepts: elif adds another test after if fails
Only the first true branch in an if/elif/else chain runs
Put stricter thresholds before broader ones

examples.title: Supply readiness
examples.explanation: 8 fails >= 10, then matches >= 5, so Review is chosen and the else is skipped.

common_mistakes: Writing else supplies < 5: instead of a bare else:
Using = instead of == in a comparison
Placing a broad threshold before a narrower one
Assuming every true-looking branch in an if/elif chain runs
Using separate if statements when exactly one result is required

exercises.title: The first matching route
exercises.prompt: What does this print? Trace from the top of the chain.
exercises.failure_message: Trace from the top. Once one condition is true, Python skips the rest of this chain.
hints: Start at the first if. Is torch_count >= 12 true when torch_count is 12?
When the first condition is true, elif and else are not checked.
12 meets the first threshold, so Long route prints.

exercises.title: Put the thresholds in order
exercises.prompt: The expedition has 14 rations and should be Cleared, but the program prints Review. Repair the decision without changing rations or the status text.
hints: The comparisons are valid. The problem is which one Python reaches first.
A value of 14 also satisfies rations >= 5.
Test the stricter >= 12 threshold before the broader >= 5 threshold.

tests.message: Use elif so the chain can test another condition after if fails.
Keep an if / elif / else decision chain.
status should end as Cleared for 14 rations.

exercises.title: Expedition status
exercises.prompt:
Create a function readiness_status(supplies) that returns:
- "Cleared" for 10 or more supplies
- "Review" for 5 through 9 supplies
- "Denied" for fewer than 5 supplies

Use one if / elif / else chain. Return the string; do not print it.
exercises.success_message: The desk can now make one clear decision from several possibilities.
hints: After the first condition fails, elif supplies >= 5 handles the middle group.
Use if supplies >= 10, then elif supplies >= 5, then else.

tests.message: Use elif so the chain can test another condition after if fails.
Use an if / elif / else chain to choose the status.

exercises.title: Threat labels
exercises.prompt:
Write threat_label(level) returning "Severe" for 8 or more, "Elevated" for 4 through 7, and "Low" otherwise.

Return the label; do not print it. Use if / elif / else.
hints: Start with the highest severity threshold.
The middle band is level >= 4 after the severe check fails.
Use if level >= 8, elif level >= 4, else for Low.

tests.message: Use elif so the chain can test another condition after if fails.
Use an if / elif / else chain.
